summary.en: Salvadoran troops are conducting strikes in Haiti, killing gang leader Mathias Saintil and demolishing the mansion of a 400‑member Mawozo gang leader. The Salvadoran president has warned Haitian gang leaders that his forces will finish them as in El Salvador, while Haitian leaders travel to El Salvador to discuss the offensive. Regional leaders, including the Dominican president, have voiced support for the Salvadoran deployment and called for better coordination of forces. Amnesty International has urged that the deployment respect human rights. The conflict produced 193 battle-related deaths in 2024, according to UCDP.
summary.nb: Salvadoranske tropper gjennomfører angrep i Haiti, dreper gjengleder Mathias Saintil og river ned herskapshuset til en leder for 400‑personers Mawozo-gjeng. Den salvadoranske presidenten har advart haitiske gjengledere om at hans styrker vil fullføre dem som i El Salvador, mens haitiske ledere reiser til El Salvador for å diskutere offensiven. Regionale ledere, inkludert den dominikanske presidenten, har uttrykt støtte til den salvadoranske innsatsen og etterlyst bedre koordinering av styrkene. Amnesty International har oppfordret til at innsatsen respekterer menneskerettighetene. Konflikten førte til 193 dødsfall i kamper i 2024, ifølge UCDP.

background.title: Haitian conflict
background.extract: Since 2020, Haiti's capital Port-au-Prince has been the site of an ongoing armed conflict between rival gangs and the state. The government of Haiti and national security forces have struggled to maintain their control of Port-au-Prince amid this conflict, with gangs speculated to control up to 90% of the city by 2023. In response to the escalating fighting, an armed vigilante movement, known as bwa kale, also emerged, with the purpose of fighting the gangs. On 2 October 2023, United Nations Security Council Resolution 2699 was approved, authorizing a Kenya-led "multinational security support mission" to Haiti. Until 2024, the war was between two major groups and their allies: the Revolutionary Forces of the G9 Family and Allies and the G-Pèp. However, in February 2024 the two rival groups united in a coalition known as Viv Ansanm, formed to oppose the government and the UN mission.
